extracted.intended_audience: biomedical researchers and grant reviewers focused on S. aureus vaccine/immunology studies
extracted.subtask_description: Design and evaluation framework to identify protective versus non-protective human antibodies to Staphylococcus aureus using a prospective human cohort, serology (65-antigen panel), functional in vitro assays, and murine adoptive-transfer models to prioritize vaccine antigen candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance of antigen (expression in human infection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detection of a high-titer antibody response (rising in convalescence, and relative to controls) confirms that an antigen is expressed during natural human infection and targeted by the host.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a broad antigen panel (65 selected SA antigens covering pathogenesis categories; surface-expressed or secreted only). Compare samples from invasive disease to non-invasive disease and healthy controls to identify antigens most relevant to invasive infection. Rising titer in convalescence relative to controls is the operational definition of in vivo expression and immunologic relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serologic measurement rigor and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Patient samples will be measured in biological and technological triplicate to ensure reproducibility of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary platform: liquid bead array technology. To maximize rigor: use extensive controls, validate with ELISA, confirm sample addition with anti-human IgG, and include negative controls (buffer and antigen tag controls) to ensure proper antigen binding/conjugation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoptive-transfer functional protection assay endpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection after adoptive transfer is assessed by bacterial burden and immunopathology measured after murine challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocol: patient sera adoptively transferred via IP route 24 hours before systemic IP challenge; assess kidney and spleen CFUs, cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α), and kidney histopathology (gross pathology and H&E to assess abscess size and numbers) at 48 hours post-challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numeric thresholds for defining serum-mediated protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for selecting sera as 'protective' or 'highly protective' are defined by quantitative reductions in CFU and immunopathology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant protection: >1 log CFU reduction and/or significant reduction in immunopathology (primary: kidney abscess size and number; secondary: cytokines). High protection: >3 log CFU reduction. Samples meeting these criteria at any timepoint advance to downstream characterization (Aim 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth of protection assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether protective sera confer protection broadly across strains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rechallenge recipients both with the same clinical isolate obtained from the infected patient and with a strain from a distinct lineage to evaluate breadth of protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appropriate murine models including humanized mice
rubrics_metrics.description: Complement wild-type mouse assays with humanized NSG mice when human tropism may affect detection of protective activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because some human-relevant factors may be missed in wild-type mice, include humanized mouse models (e.g., UCLA CFAR core NSG mice) as part of the initial screen and for confirmatory assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject enrollment and sampling timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Define target human cohorts and sample collection windows to capture the relevant humoral response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target populations: children (1–17 years) and older adults (>65 years). Obtain sera and PBMCs within 48 hours of growth of SA in culture and at multiple timepoints up to 12 months post-infection (example timepoints: V1 acute, V2 4–6 weeks (peak), V3 6 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical power, analysis plan, and significance thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample size and analysis parameters chosen to identify antigen–protection associations with adequate power and multiple-testing correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planned enrollment: 100 subjects (75 children, 25 older adults). Expectation: ~50% non-protective, 40% moderately protective, 10% highly protective sera. Power: 80% to detect ≥1.9-fold increase in odds of protection per SD titer increase. Analysis: logistic regression with antibody levels as continuous variables. Significance threshold adjusted conservatively to 0.001 (Bonferroni-type correction for 65 antigens).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancement criteria from Aim 1 to Aim 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples are advanced for deeper characterization based on in vivo functional protection metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance sera that show significant protection at any timepoint per the defined numeric thresholds (>1 log CFU reduction and/or reduced immunopathology). These advanced samples will undergo structural and functional profiling and be candidates for reverse vaccine development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antibody functional/structural characterization battery
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterize candidate protective and non-protective antibodies using complementary in vitro and in vivo assays plus structural profiling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planned assays include in vitro bacterial killing, cytotoxicity assays, opsonophagocytic killing (OPK) assays, binding/competition assays, structural analyses (epitope mapping, B cell receptor sequencing), and confirmatory adoptive transfer to both wild-type and humanized mouse models. Profile Fab and Fc features (e.g., glycosylation/sialylation) that correlate with protection or non-protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational definition of antigen 'subdominant' status for vaccine targeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify antigens with little humoral imprint as candidate vaccine targets to avoid interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subdominant antigens are those showing low antibody titers after SA exposure; hypothesis is that targeting subdominant antigens (little prior imprint) may circumvent vaccine interference observed with dominant antigens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria/demonstrations for antibody-mediated interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and detect mechanisms by which pre-existing non-protective antibodies interfere with vaccine- or mAb-mediated protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two demonstrated mechanisms: (1) immune imprinting/original antigenic sin — vaccination recalls ineffective memory responses from prior infection; (2) direct antibody competition — co-transfer or co-incubation of non-protective human antibodies reduces efficacy of protective antibodies. Demonstrate interference via competitive binding assays, mixed-opsonophagocytic killing assays, and in vivo co-transfer protection studies (e.g., reduced protection when protective and non-protective Abs are mixed at physiologic molar ratios).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay validation and controls for bead-array serology
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure integrity of antigen coupling and signal specificity in multiplex serology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls: anti-human IgG to confirm sample addition; buffer and antigen tag negative controls to ensure proper antigen conjugation; technical reproducibility and validation by ELISA to avoid false negatives from improper antigen conjugation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal kinetics as part of protective response evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish and use defined temporal windows to capture peak protective antibody responses after infection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary data indicate peak reduction in SA CFU occurs at 4–6 weeks post-infection (V2). Sera collected at V2 (6 weeks) are prioritized for initial adoptive-transfer screening; follow-up timepoints can be assessed if initial protection is observed.
